messages:
Maria: Heads up — since ~03:40 UTC we started seeing requests from EU-prod-tier customers routed to us in us-west-2. Short thread with findings.

Jay: Seeing increased p95 for eu-region routes, spikes align with a model variant failing in eu. Logs show fallback policy triggered to 'closest-compatible' which picked us-west.

Devon: The problem: fallback policy is 'region-preference but allow cross-region fallback' and circuit breaking only on connection errors, not on high-latency responses. Health checks didn't flag degraded tails.

Maria: TL;DR fallback loop: eu request -> eu model variant returns slow 504-ish -> fallback to us-west variant -> us-west capacity thickens -> smart router sees eu latency and routes back to eu after TTL -> repeat.

Oliver: I can see router logs: key: route_id=rt-42, decision_chain=[eu->fallback(us-west)->backoff->eu], repeated 6x per request. Example log line: 
```
2026-03-09T03:41:12Z router decision route=rt-42 src=eu-1 dest=us-west-3 reason=fallback_variant_selected latency_ms=1587 attempts=1
```

Anna: We also saw the quota-metering misclassifying some reserved pool capacity as available, which allowed fallbacks to oversubscribe us-west.

Maria: Immediate mitigation I pushed: disabled cross-region fallback for prod-tier (policy toggle) and bumped fallback backoff TTL to 10s. That reduced cross-region churn. :thumbsup:

Jay: Good. Next steps: add latency-based circuit breaker at router level (reject fallback when observed 95th>1000ms for 30s), add health probe to mark 'degraded' when tail latency > median*4, and add metric to console dashboard.

Devon: Proposed API change: allow rollout config to specify 'fallback_safety' flags: { allow_cross_region: bool, max_fallback_hops: int, latency_threshold_ms: int }. Example:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/rt-42
{"fallback_safety": {"allow_cross_region": false, "max_fallback_hops": 2, "latency_threshold_ms": 800}}
```

Oliver: Also add telemetry event on fallback decision carrying last 5 latencies to make loops traceable end-to-end.

Anna: For UX: console should surface a "fallback health" signal per route and warn during canary rollouts when fallback_safety isn't set. We had a canary where the new variant used a slower kernel — this would've prevented the cross-region swing.

Maria: ACTIONS: Jay to add dashboard tile and alert, Devon to add API schema change ticket, Oliver to patch router logs, Anna to draft console UX warning. I'll coordinate with support for affected customers and send a short status email.

Jay: I'm posting the temporary feature flag here: ff:cross_region_fallback_prod=false. Will rollback after the router fix lands.

Devon: Noted: we should run a chaos test covering 'variant-slow' that forces high token-generation latency and validate router behavior (and assert no cross-region fallback).

Oliver: Follow-up infra note: we may need a global quota reconciliation to avoid pool miscounts — Anna, can you check reserved pool accounting?

Anna: On it. Found a race where capacity_reconcile didn't subtract transient fallback reservations. Opening PR with a fix + unit test.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye on alerts and notify impacted customers if they reappear.

Maria: Thanks everyone. Will keep thread updated. If anyone sees residual cross-region errors, ping @oncall-sre or drop here.
